key_insight: A learned convolution-based flux closure can predict atmospheric boundary layer momentum and heat fluxes more accurately than a standard K-profile model while remaining interpretable.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical, transparent subgrid parameterization for coarse weather and climate models, especially in unstable and stable boundary layers where traditional closures struggle.
method: Train linearized convolution operators on LES-generated nondimensional mean profiles and fluxes.
Test multiple first-order closure variants using temperature and velocity profile combinations.
Select the best model by lowest mean squared error and validate in posteriori single-column simulations.
evidence_signal: The model was trained and evaluated on high-resolution LES across multiple stability regimes, then tested on unseen cases and in posteriori single-column runs where it remained stable and closely matched LES profiles.
watch_item: Performance depends on LES-derived training data and idealized homogeneous-surface conditions, so transferability to complex terrain and real-world heterogeneity still needs validation.
paper_title: Data-Driven Flux Parameterization for the Atmospheric Boundary Layer
